question: Butane ( {C}₄{H}₁₀ ) exists in two different forms: one with a straight chain and one with a branched chain. What is this phenomenon called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Isomerism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isomerism** is the phenomenon where compounds have the **same molecular formula but different structural or spatial arrangements**, resulting in different physical and/or chemical properties.
 
• Butane (**C₄H₁₀**) exists in two isomeric forms:
 
 
• **n-Butane:** A straight-chain structure where all four carbon atoms are connected in a linear arrangement.
 
• **Isobutane (2-methylpropane):** A branched-chain structure where three carbon atoms form the main chain, and one carbon atom is attached as a branch.
 
 
 
• The difference in their structure leads to **variations in boiling points, melting points, and other properties**, despite having the same molecular formula.
 
• Isomerism is broadly classified into **structural isomerism** (differences in connectivity of atoms) and **stereoisomerism** (differences in spatial arrangement).
 
• In the case of butane, the isomerism exhibited is specifically **structural isomerism**, more precisely, **chain isomerism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Catenation:**

 
 
• **Catenation** refers to the ability of an element, particularly carbon, to form long chains or rings by bonding with atoms of the same element.
 
• It is a unique property of carbon due to its **tetravalency** and strong **covalent bonding**.
 
• While catenation enables the formation of compounds like butane, it does not explain the existence of its isomers.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation:**
 
 
• **Sublimation** is a physical process where a substance transitions directly from the **solid state to the gaseous state** without passing through the liquid state.
 
• Examples include substances like iodine and dry ice (solid carbon dioxide).
 
• This phenomenon is unrelated to the structural variation of butane.
 
 
 
• **Polymerisation:**
 
 
• **Polymerisation** is a chemical process in which **small molecules (monomers)** combine to form a large molecule (polymer).
 
• For example, ethene undergoes polymerisation to form polyethylene.
 
• Butane is a simple hydrocarbon and does not undergo polymerisation in the context of the given question.
 
 
 
• **Chain Isomerism in Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• Chain isomerism occurs when compounds with the same molecular formula have **different arrangements of their carbon skeletons**.
 
• In butane, n-butane and isobutane differ in their carbon chain structures.
 
• This is a type of structural isomerism and is commonly observed in hydrocarbons.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of Isomers:**

 
 
• Isomers are widely used in the **pharmaceutical industry**. For example, different isomers of a drug can have different therapeutic effects.
 
• In the **petroleum industry**, isomers like isobutane are used to improve the octane rating of fuels.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Isomerism:**
 
 
• **Ethyl alcohol (C₂H₆O)** and **dimethyl ether (C₂H₆O)** are examples of functional isomers.
 
• Glucose and fructose are examples of structural isomers in the carbohydrate family.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Structural Isomerism:**
 
 
• Structural isomerism explains variations in **physical properties like boiling and melting points**, and **chemical reactivity**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in organic chemistry, especially in the study of hydrocarbons and functional groups.
